title: Emergency order by US to 'prevent blackouts' could affect data centres
source_used: The National (with TD World for the order dates)
key_facts: The US Department of Energy issued an emergency order to try to prevent blackouts amid surging electricity demand; it stays in effect until 16 Oct (TD World: 13 to 16 Oct 2026).
The order prompted PJM Interconnection to direct data centres and other large-load customers to switch to back-up generation if necessary.
The department cited a high rate of planned generator outages in the autumn maintenance season as a possible blackout trigger.
The department said the US has 35 GW of unused back-up generation nationwide.
PJM issued a maximum generation alert for 13 and 14 Oct as above-normal temperatures were forecast, and said the alert does not require any action from customers.
Energy Secretary Chris Wright said the order will help ensure millions of American families and businesses across the mid-Atlantic have affordable, reliable and secure electricity.
TD World adds that the order (No. 202-26-50) covers 13 states and Washington, D.C., and lets PJM use back-up generation as a last resort before declaring the top-level Energy Emergency Alert 3.
Data centres are widely blamed for rising US electricity prices, and the warnings come before the midterm elections.
